card.name: Verbs right before a duration or delay
card.fires_on: A verb or noun that sits just before a span of time, such as 'for 2 weeks' or 'until several hours'. It is common after 'may not be' or 'may not' and 'can' (achieved, occur, persist, appear).

modes.label: Delayed onset
modes.description: Verb after 'may not' that points to a wait before an effect appears.
modes.example: may not<< occur>> until several hours following ingestion.

modes.label: Lasting effect
modes.description: Verb or word before a duration describing how long something lasts.
modes.example: relief may result within 6 to 48 hours and<< persist>> for several days to two weeks.

modes.label: Duration after a noun
modes.description: A noun or 'for' that leads into a length of time.
modes.example: your refrigerator will stay at the proper<< temperature>> for about four hours

card.writes: It suppresses 'until' and 'till', so it steers the next word toward 'for' plus a time span instead of 'until'.
card.plain: It marks a spot where the text is about to say how long something lasts or how long until it starts.
